Alloy ingots with a nominal composition of Co40Ni30Cr20Al5Ti5 (a.t. %) were fabricated using a vacuum suspension melting furnace under a high-purity argon atmosphere. To ensure compositional homogeneity, each ingot was remelted at least five times and cast into water-cooled copper molds (50 mm diameter, 45 mm height).
The cast ingots were sectioned into thin sheets with a thickness of 4.5 mm and homogenized at 1150 ◦C for 2 h to eliminate elemental segregation during solidification.
Subsequently, the homogenized sheets were cold-rolled to a total thickness reduction of 65 % through multiple passes, with a reduction of 5–10 % per pass.
The deformed sheets underwent static recrystallization at 1150 ◦C for 2 min, followed by aging at 800 ◦C for 4 h to promote precipitation.
